plan.title: Condition-specific time-course RNA-seq: DESeq2 interaction analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0-t3) x 3 replicates (n=25 samples with metadata columns condition, time, time_hours), human cell line, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 25 samples). The research question - which genes change over time in a condition-specific way, beyond the shared time trend - is a DESeq2 interaction (condition:time) question, not a simple two-group contrast. T1S1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) on the raw counts to confirm the 8 condition x time cells separate and to catch outliers or a mislabelled sample before any model is fit; time is treated as a categorical factor (t0/t1/t2/t3) since only 4 timepoints are given, avoiding an unwarranted linear-time assumption. T1S2 fits the DESeq2 negative-binomial model with design ~condition + time + condition:time (median-of-ratios normalization built into the model, explicit reference levels for both factors), tests each condition:time interaction coefficient (t1,t2,t3 vs t0) with the Wald test, shrinks the interaction log2 fold changes with apeglm, and applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05 - this directly answers 'condition-specific change beyond the shared time trend' because the interaction term is by construction the deviation from the additive (shared) time effect. T1S3 clusters the genes with any significant interaction term into trajectory groups from the per-timepoint condition-vs-condition log2 fold changes, and reports MA/dispersion diagnostics, the p-value histogram, and the reproducibility record, per DESeq2 time-course reporting practice. T2S1 runs GO biological-process over-representation (clusterProfiler enrichGO, universe = tested genes, rrvgo term reduction) on the significant interaction gene list, following the knowledge service's ruling for this design (LRT and preranked fgsea on a Wald/LRT statistic from an interaction design are flagged methods here; ORA on the significant gene list is the permitted enrichment method), with MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome/WikiPathways over-representation run in parallel as secondary collections using the same universe and size window. A caveat is carried through explicitly: if fewer than ~50 genes reach significance, ORA has little power and the enrichment step reports set size and interprets cautiously rather than over-reading sparse results.
